Open relaxation guide
Vision Guardian · End-of-day break
Spine Guardian · End-of-day relaxation
Pause your screen task and relax your face. Blink gently and naturally without squeezing, pressing or rubbing your eyes.

Look away from this screen at something about 6 metres away for at least 20 seconds. Repeat screen breaks during the day: every 20 minutes, look 20 feet away for 20 seconds. No need to stretch your eyes to their limits.

Adjust text size, glare and screen position before returning. This guide supports comfortable breaks; it does not treat myopia or dry-eye disease. Persistent discomfort needs an eye-care assessment. Eye-pressure and extreme-gaze exercises are not offered.
For general relaxation only. After CDR, other neck surgery or with a cervical condition, follow your care team’s instructions instead. Sit with your feet and back supported; breathe naturally.
Let your shoulders settle. If comfortable, make gentle shoulder circles without forcing your neck, then pause. No deep pressure, pulling or prescribed range is needed.

Change position and bring the screen to a comfortable height with your arms supported. Stop for increasing pain, dizziness, numbness or weakness and seek advice. Chin-tuck training, deep neck pressure and traction await professional review.
